Hi Dana — great to hear from you and thanks for the doc. High-level options below; I put a short reasoning line for each so you can share with legal/finance.

Option A — HSM-seat (recommended for steady high-volume crypto ops)
- Commercial: one-time onboarding + monthly HSM-seat fee (covers dedicated slot and management).
- Billing: seat fee + standard per-token inference usage.
- Crediting: we typically amortize onboarding across committed usage; for a 36-month commit we can offer a 20–30% credit on the residency add-on for year 1 to offset legal/enablement costs.
- When to pick: predictable, low-latency key operations and audited control is primary.

Option B — Per-request KMS (recommended if crypto usage is spiky)
- Commercial: no seat; per-key-request fee layered on top of usage.
- Billing: more variable; lower fixed costs, higher marginal cost.
- Credit: we can tier the per-request price so top-tier committed customers get volume-break discounts; less scope for one-time credits.

Audit log retention
- 1 year retention included. Extended retention to 7 years is an add-on priced by GB/month. For large commits we can offer a 50% discount on retention fees for the first 12 months or convert retention fees into a fixed line item in the SOW and apply credits.

Residency modeling
- Two approaches: flat monthly residency fee (simpler) or blended residency credit where we amortize a portion of the residency fee into per-token pricing given a usage commitment. For a 3-year commit we can do a blended model that reduces the visible monthly residency line by up to 30% in year 1.

Next steps
- I’ll run the numbers with finance and legal. Can you confirm: target commit (USD M ARR), preferred HSM model (seat vs per-call), and whether MediSync expects Redwood to accept a pass-through of any third-party HSM vendor fees?

I attached a quick snapshot of current list pricing. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call Monday to walk through.

Subject: Proposed commercial options — residency, HSM, and audit retention (MediSync)

Hi Dana and team — thanks for the patience while we pulled numbers together. Below are two clean options you can review with legal/finance. I’ve also attached a short PDF that summarizes costs and the proposed SOW line items.

Option 1 (Preferred for predictability) — HSM-seat + blended residency
- Term: 36 months commit (Target: $2.4M ARR).
- HSM: two dedicated HSM seats at $6,500/seat/month. One-time onboarding $18,000.
- Residency: blended model — flat residency fee $9,000/month reduced by a 25% year-1 credit (applied as a monthly credit across your account).
- Audit logs: 7-year retention priced at $0.30/GB/month; we apply a one-time implementation credit of $25,000 to offset evidence collection and initial export.
- Commercial concessions: 12% total discount on list prices applied across token usage for the first 12 months.

Option 2 (Lower upfront, higher variable) — Per-call KMS + residency flat fee
- Term: 36 months commit.
- KMS: per-request pricing $0.00012 per key operation with volume tiers ( >100M requests/month drops to $0.00008).
- Residency: flat fee $9,000/month, no front-loaded credit; we can offer 6 months of waived retention fees as an alternative.
- Audit logs: same per-GB pricing; no implementation credit.

Other notes
- Third-party HSM passthrough: if MediSync requires a specific HSM vendor with pass-through fees, we will list the vendor fee on the SOW as a pass-through.
- DocuSign & next steps: If either option looks good I’ll circulate a redline-friendly SOW and DocuSign link. For audit evidence we can set a joint timeline: security questionnaire answers in 7 business days, initial SOC evidence delivery within 30 days of contract execution.

Please confirm which option is closer to your preference and any items you want reworked. Happy to set a 30-min call Thursday to finalize.
